page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. Provisioned via the KVM hypervisor, this instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory allocation is set at 32 GB, representing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory distribution of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is provided via AES instructions alongside AVX and AVX-512 extensions. The server does not bundle local storage, requiring attached cloud storage disks, and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without included GPUs or public IPv4 addresses.

Performance testing positions the hardware within lower-to-moderate throughput brackets relative to modern cloud compute platforms. Geekbench evaluations yield 928 in single-core performance and 3,534 in multi-core metrics, aligning with the stress-ng results of 1,100.18 and 5,879.59 respectively. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression deliver 19.11 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression processes 28.94 GB/sec. Memory subsystems demonstrate stable large-block uncached read speeds of 40.42 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 35.62 GB/sec, though small-block cached throughput and PassMark memory metrics reflect entry-level performance. Database simulation on PassMark records 2,200.81 operations, Redis SET benchmarks register 5.73 million operations per second, and network static web serving registers 4.53 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the ecs.sn2ne.2xlarge prioritizes dedicated compute allocation and conventional memory density rather than cutting-edge instructions per cycle. As an older processor model, its per-core computational throughput is limited compared to later Intel generations, meaning intensive processing tasks like medium-scale model inference perform poorly. However, the consistent dedicated thread model and steady memory bandwidth present a stable baseline for moderate operational loads. This server profile fits enterprise backend services, standard web applications, intermediate caching tiers, dev/test staging environments, and asynchronous message queue processing where balanced resources are required without requiring maximum compute density.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Built on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 32 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX and AVX-512 extensions alongside a 35 MB L3 cache. It incorporates no bundled local storage and supplies a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations reflect older-generation execution speeds, with Geekbench single-core scoring 928 and multi-core reaching 3534, placing CPU performance largely in lower percentiles. The platform delivers balanced uncached memory throughput but reduced execution efficiency on heavy compression and intensive compute tasks. Consequently, ecs.sn2ne.2xlarge is appropriate for general enterprise workloads, application backends, staging environments, and basic caching servers that require dedicated core allocation without intense per-thread compute demands.
